 Follow Black Lab Doesn’t Understand Daylight Saving Time and Her ‘Late’ Dinner Feels Like a Personal Betrayal
 Dai Poole Wed, November 4, 2026 at 2:30 AM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Gabriel Mello / Getty Images Daylight saving time may give humans an extra hour of sleep when the clocks fall back, but someone forgot to explain the arrangement to our dogs. Their internal clocks aren't hanging on the kitchen wall, and they're definitely not checking the time on a phone before deciding they're hungry.
 A Black Lab named Poppy made that very clear after the recent time change. In a hilarious video shared by @theblacklabrador_poppy , she stands patiently waiting for dinner while staring at her mom with the saddest, most betrayed expression imaginable. According to the clock, Poppy is early. According to Poppy's stomach, dinner is already unforgivably late.

 Poppy's Stomach Didn't Get the Daylight Saving Time Memo
 There's no barking, jumping or dramatic temper tantrum required to understand what Poppy is thinking. She simply stands there and stares. And somehow, that makes it even funnier.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The video pairs her increasingly tragic-looking wait with Sinéad O'Connor's "Nothing Compares 2 U," turning a one-hour dinner delay into what feels like the longest period of suffering any Labrador has ever endured.
 Poppy's mom tries to explain that the clocks went back, but the pup doesn't appear particularly interested in humanity's timekeeping decisions. Her face seems to have one question: If it's dinner time in my stomach, why isn't there food in my bowl?
 Apparently, plenty of other dogs spent the weekend asking the same thing. "Our Labrador gets very upset when the clocks fall back, but she is a great Spring forwarder," one viewer joked.
 Another summed up the entire problem perfectly: "Stomach clocks don't do daylight savings." One dog parent said they normally start dinner at 4:50, only for their pup to begin barking at 3:50 after the clocks changed. They eventually felt so bad that the dog scored a slice of cheese.
 Advertisement Advertisement Honestly, that sounds like a successful negotiation strategy.
 Related: Cat Treats That Look Like Tiny Lollipops Just Earned a Major Pet Industry Honor 
 Labradors Take Their Schedules Very Seriously
 Dogs may not understand what an hour means on a clock, but they can become remarkably good at anticipating routines. Meals, walks and bedtime all come with patterns and cues that have nothing to do with the numbers displayed on our phones.
 For food-motivated Labs in particular, messing with dinner time can certainly look like a major breach of trust.
 We've seen Labradors bring this same level of commitment to other important matters. Stella and Mabel apparently waited all year for their chance to hide in a giant pile of fall leaves , while another Labrador Retriever showed exactly how seriously the breed can take food when he settled in to enjoy his very own breakfast burrito .
 Advertisement Advertisement Poppy's dilemma also prompted viewers to share one practical idea: gradually shifting a pet's schedule around the clock change rather than expecting them to suddenly wait an extra hour.
 But Poppy may have inspired an even simpler solution. One commenter suggested that when the clocks fall back, a "real lab" should receive two meals: one at the old dinner time and another at the new one. Something tells us Poppy wouldn't object.
